_comment: Paste these into Integrations → Data Layer → Page patterns for an Akinon site.
They replace the built-in `akinon` platform profile, whose defaults do not
match real Project Zero routing. The profile assumes /(p|urun)/,
/(c|kategori)/, /(sepet|cart) and /(search|arama) — so with the defaults the
cart and search page types are NEVER detected on any Akinon storefront.
Verified against:
pz_classic_project/omnife_base/urls.py            → path('list/', ListView, name='search')
pz_classic_project/omnife_project/omnife/products/urls.py → products/<pk>/
pz_classic_project/omnife_base/baskets/urls.py    → baskets/basket/
pz_next_project/src/routes/index.ts        → BASKET='/baskets/basket', LIST='/list'
pz_next_project/src/app/.../product/[pk]   → /product/<pk>
pz_next_project/src/app/.../category/[pk]  → /category/<pk>
pz_next_project/src/views/header/search    → /list/?search_text=
IMPORTANT — pretty URLs. Omnitron can rewrite product and category URLs to
arbitrary SEO slugs (@akinon/next/middlewares/pretty-url.ts), which no regex
can enumerate. That affects only the page-type LABEL, not product identity:
Selwise reads the product code from the PDP's JSON-LD `sku`, which both
stacks emit, so product events stay correct on a pretty URL. If page-type
labelling matters for a campaign's targeting, add that project's own slug
pattern here (e.g. "-p-[0-9]+$").
The `search` pattern deliberately requires the query parameter: /list/ with
no search_text is a category listing, not a search.
